title: Finite clopen decomposition of pro-etale derived coefficient categories
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and coefficient datum $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $\mathcal O_E$, $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$, as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be a finite family of pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes covering $X$, with inclusions $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], finite constructibility [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], integral categories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

For $R=(A_{E,n})_X$ or $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], restriction gives an exact equivalence of module-sheaf categories
$$
 \operatorname{Mod}(R)\simeq\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Mod}(R|_{X_i}).
$$
Its quasi-inverse sends $(F_i)_i$ to the sheaf $U\mapsto\prod_i F_i(U\times_X X_i)$, with componentwise restriction maps and module operations. Applying these functors to complexes induces the equivalence of their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with cohomology and derived tensor computed componentwise. Restriction preserves the coefficient tensor unit, finite coefficient reduction, strict towers of coefficient modules and their derived inverse limits [def-weil-derived-limit].

For every $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, these equivalences, followed at field stages by the rationalized and common-stage constructions of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], restrict to equivalences
$$
 D^b_c(X,\Lambda)\simeq\prod_{i\in I}D^b_c(X_i,\Lambda),\qquad
 D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)\simeq\prod_{i\in I}D^b_{ctf}(X_i,\Lambda).
$$
The latter respects tensor products and tensor units. At finite level the cohomological and Tor bounds may be chosen to be any common bounds for the finitely many components; at integral level the same holds for the bounds uniform in all reductions. The equivalences respect coefficient reduction and scalar extension. The empty family is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and the product category has its unique object and morphism.

proof.text: Use the unchanged canonical coefficient data and proved support calculations from the extracted finite-clopen decomposition core. This compilation split preserves the complete original argument below and the current finite restriction identification proof.

Apply the normalized module gluing theorem, package its unit and counit as an equivalence, and retain its explicit sectionwise product, scalar, restriction and morphism formulas. The field coefficient map to each stalk preserves the unit witnessing invertibility of the coefficient prime. The covering equality handles the empty case.

Use the finite-product derived calculus for the unbounded equivalence and exact-functor cohomology comparison. Restriction sends the regular module directly to the restricted regular module. Compare each published duality-model tensor with the native K-flat tensor by fully faithful localization whiskering, and compose these model comparisons with the bifunctor isomorphism supplied by normalized clopen K-flat monoidal descent.

Use finite pullback localization/cohomology to identify exact restriction with actual finite pullback, followed by normalized coefficient transport. Apply the fixed-interval finite constructibility and Tor criteria and choose common bounds over the finite index set. Exact restriction preserves products, so the signed additive Roos comparison also gives the strict tower comparison.

The constructible integral, rational, common-stage and finite-Tor equivalences remain unproved in finiteClopen_constructible_equivalences. Retain the planned completed-system, integral-descent and field-stage dependencies for that original hole. The independent proof of the integral restriction identification constructs scalar transport along the canonical completed-ring isomorphism and composes exact-derived-functor comparisons with the normalized open-completed comparison on constructible objects.

The finite restriction identification is proved by taking the inverse of the canonical finite coefficient ring comparison supplied by finite pullback localization/cohomology. Scalar restriction along this isomorphism is an exact equivalence. Descend it degreewise, combine the exact-derived composition and natural-isomorphism comparisons with the normalized finite pullback comparison, and retain the localization factorization on complexes. The scalar-extension proof composes the normalized completion-unit isomorphisms with the ordinary scalar/pullback square, and uses the published rational pullback object and Hom formulas. The unit proof transports regular module units through normalized finite and completed restriction, then applies rationalization and common-stage inclusions.
